text:
A: Hiya! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, loud and clear. I'm Gemma.
A: Claire. Lovely to meet you. I'll be honest, I've sort of forgotten what we're meant to talk about. Did they say?
B: I don't think they said anything. Just chat for three minutes, I think.
A: Oh good, I can do that. Did you do that puzzle thing at the start? I got completely stuck on the third one and just stared at it.
B: The shapes one? I quite enjoyed it, to be fair. I worked it out on a bit of paper.
A: See, that's organised. I just turned my head sideways a lot. Erm, so where are you calling from?
B: Peterborough. Werrington, on the edge.
A: Oh right. I'm in Otley, near Leeds. I saw your dog lead on the hook in your photo, actually. Have you got a dog?
B: Lurcher. Pip.
A: No! I've got a lurcher! Biscuit. He's a rescue, very scruffy, steals socks off the radiator and takes them in the garden like trophies.
B: Pip ate a tea towel last week.
A: A whole tea towel?
B: Most of it. Vet said just keep an eye, and it came out the other end fine. Not the nicest Saturday morning, mind.
A: Oh god. They're daft, aren't they? Lovely, but daft. Do you take her out much?
B: Ferry Meadows most days. I do the parkrun there on Saturdays as well, so she gets dragged round after.
A: Ooh, a parkrun. I'm not a runner. I walk Biscuit up the Chevin, which is a big hill above Otley, and that's about as athletic as I get. I do the wild swimming in summer, but that's mostly standing in a river going "it's freezing, it's freezing" for ten minutes.
B: Rather you than me, honestly. What do you do for work, then?
A: Speech and language therapist, with kids. NHS, so I go round clinics and primary schools in Leeds three days a week. Mostly little ones who aren't talking yet, or not very clearly, and you play with them on the floor and try to work out what's going on. And then I go home and don't do my paperwork, which is the bit I'm terrible at. Sorry, that's a lot. What about you?
B: Quality engineer. We make engines and generators. When a supplier sends us parts that fail inspection, I'm the one who works out why, and then I sit in a meeting with them while they try to tell me it's not their fault.
A: Oh, I bet you're good at that.
B: I just keep asking for the data. They give up eventually.
A: Ha! I love that. Did you go to uni for it, or...?
B: Apprenticeship at sixteen, then college on day release, then I did my degree part-time at night in my late twenties. Work paid.
A: At night, while working? That's proper graft. I started an MA once and dropped it after a year because I kept reading the interesting bits instead of doing the essays.
B: That's the trouble with interesting bits, to be fair.
A: Exactly! Do you know what I mean, you go off down a rabbit hole and suddenly it's March. Sorry, where was I?
B: Your MA, which you didn't finish.
A: Ha, yes, thank you. One day, I keep telling Mark that.
